[quote=tartakum;60329672][nation]Qianxun[/nation] What do you think my profits will be after a few months after the oil wells are complete.[/quote]
(C$ = Commonwealth dollars, Vespuria's old currency. I don't remember what his new currency is called, but I'll be using this because it's exactly the same value as the IRL US dollar)

I mean, it's not clear considering that I only offered an outline for how the oil rigs would be constructed. 

For maybe the first two years of operation, you're not going to obtain any profit from operating the oil rigs, since you'll be using revenues from Tencor to pay back the debt you owe Qianxun and Elseyro-Vespurian creditors. After that though, you'll obtain a modest enough profit I guess.

We only started with five oil rigs, so let's surmise that's something like 20,000 barrels per day when things go well. Since you're being attacked by pirates every now and then (and decided to not commission me for ships smh) we'll bump that down to something like 18,000 barrels per day. (20,000 x .9 = 18,000 which is 90% efficiency). 

18,000 x 5 for the five oil rigs = 90,000 barrels per day.
90,000 barrels per day * 30 days = 2,700,000 barrels per month.

I have no idea what the price per barrel of oil is on Erene, but according to Bob and a few others, it's like IRL, so C$60-70. For clarity's sake, we'll go with C$65 per barrel. Now, since you made the wise decision of selecting an authoritarian socialist state with an abysmal human rights record, we can go as low as C$15 per barrel as the operating costs, but since I have a reputation to uphold and because we had to field some University faculty for the oil rigs, we'll just guesstimate operating costs to be C$25 per barrel.

2,700,000 barrels per month x C$65 = C$175,500,000 monthly revenue
2,700,000 barrels per month x C$25 = C$67,500,000 monthly operating costs

C$175,500,000 - C$67,500,000 = [b]C$108,000,000 in monthly profits from these five oil rigs[/b]. Once we add the remaining 14 oil rigs, you can imagine this number jumping really high.

Now, Tencor is currently C$1.9 billion in debt. This debt was from the capital that Qianxun, Almstedt Corporation, several Tarta investors, and a few kinda corrupt MZP politicians gave ECG/Tencor to construct those oil rigs. Since we're allies now, let's imagine that I allow debt servicing to stay low, maybe C$20,000,000 per month that Tencor will have to pay to creditors. That means that the company will have debt for around 8 years, give or take. If things go well with the SEZs, we can even considering waiving part of the debt or pay it ourselves.

Next let's reduce the profits by a further C$18,000,000 per month to pay for corporate costs. So this would be payments made to corporate executives, for their offices, staff, marketing, legal, and most importantly a savings account for the remaining oil rigs we still need to build.

You now have C$70,000,000 a month. That's your final profit. BUT.

That isn't your money. 40% goes to Tencor, 60% goes to the National Wealth Fund. That 60% is now the Republic of Tartakum's money. That's C$42,000,000 a month or C$500 million a year. All that money is then transferred to the NWF to be reinvested in a diverse stock portfolio.

You set the SWF's initial capital to C$2 billion, now C$500 million is added to that per year. The value of the SWF [i]should[/i] rise as you start receiving dividends from your investments. Again, I'll just guessing here, but let's say for your first year in which you start receiving profits, you collect C$200,000,000 from the SWF's investments (That's an 8% profit for 2 billion dollars + 500 million from oil profits).

That money isn't your money, it gets reinvested back into the SWF, letting it grow and grow as it collects more and more assets. Remember how in a previous post I set your withdrawal to 3% of the SWF's value? In your first year making profits, that's [b]C$75,000,000 per year[/b] that you can withdraw and add you your government budget, which in all honesty isn't a lot. But that's at the SWF's current value. In half a decade, ten years? Maybe the SWF grows to such a size that this starts becoming a fairly big core of your budget.

And of course, if you want we can always negotiate replacing the 3% withdrawal limit with something else so you can yoink more of the money immediately, but I would advise against that for now.
